priorities in 2026
General Objective 1: A new plan for Europe's
sustainable prosperity and competitiveness
Specific Objective 1.1: Fostering the EU's Scientific and
Technological Progress
To reduce strategic dependencies and ensure diversified, secure supply chains, the EU must
further advance its scientific and technological progress. In recent years, DG RTD has successfully
embedded R&I priorities into the European Semester process. The 2025 Semester cycle marked
a significant achievement, with R&I-related investments and reforms highlighted in the country-
specific recommendations for 26 out of 27 Member States, an unprecedented level of recognition
of R&I as a key driver of competitiveness, productivity and long-term growth. In 2026, DG RTD
will maintain this high level of engagement to ensure that R&I continues to drive national reform
and investment priorities. Enhanced Dialogues
R&I investments and reforms. Additional dialogues between Member States and DG RTD are
planned in 2026 to provide targeted guidance, foster mutual learning and strengthen alignment
between national and EU R&I priorities. To bridge the innovation, divide and enhance regional
administrative and implementation capacity and create a well-connected European innovation
ecosystem that leaves no region behind, a new Memorandum of Understanding will be signed
with the Committee of the Regions and new regions will receive the Regional Innovation Valleys
label. The Policy Support Facility (PSF) will also continue to provide independent, high-level
expertise to assist national policymakers in designing and implementing effective R&I reforms. A
new PSF framework contract expected to be signed in early 2026, will enable enhanced support
activities throughout the year.
A strategic priority for 2026 is implementing the European Strategy for Artificial
Intelligence (AI) in Science (1). As AI rapidly reshapes the global research landscape, Europe
must maintain its scientific leadership while ensuring that AI development remains human-
centric, trustworthy, and aligned with European values. The cornerstone of this transformation
will be the operationalisation of RAISE (Resource for AI Science in Europe), a virtual European
institute that pools and coordinates essential AI resources across the continent. Following the
establishment of the RAISE Secretariat, a call for a Scientific Advisory Board will be launched
in 2026. Building on the successful RAISE pilot, the first full operational measures will deploy
Networks of Excellence and Doctoral Networks under the "Choose Europe" initiative to
attract, train, and retain top AI and scientific talent. RAISE will provide enhanced dedicated access
for researchers and start-ups to AI resources, supported by Horizon Europe funding and secured
access to AI Gigafactories. Implementation will proceed through close collaboration with Member
States, associated countries, and stakeholders within the European Research Area governance
framework, ensuring coherence with the Apply AI Strategy (2) through structured coordination
mechanisms. To ensure these efforts remain aligned with Europe's commitment to ethical AI in
science, the European Group on Ethics in Science and New Technologies (EGE) (3) will
deliver a comprehensive opinion on AI in science, as well as a statement on the ethical aspects
6

of AI-enabled neurotechnology. This work is essential to AI-driven research is human-centric,
explainable, and trustworthy. DG RTD will also contribute to the Cloud and AI Development
Act, to be adopted in 2026, which will strengthen Europe's capabilities in cloud computing and
artificial intelligence infrastructure.
Specific Objective 1.2: Accelerating the conversion of
emerging research into transformative innovation that is
commercialised and scaled up in the EU
Competitiveness Compass for
the EU (4), DG RTD will implement the EU Startup and Scaleup Strategy (5) adopted in 2025,
making s
that Europes scientific excellence translates into prosperity, technological sovereignty and
sustainable growth. In 2026, DG RTD will drive the European Innovation Act, a key pillar of
Startup and Scaleup strategy that will shape a truly integrated and innovation-friendly Single
Market. The Act will tackle persistent challenges including fragmented regulation, limited
academia-industry collaboration, and underinvestment in commercialisation by building more
agile and coordinated pathways for innovation across the EU. It will do so by pooling national,
European and private investments, unlocking the potential of intellectual property rights, and
improving access to talent, markets and technology and research infrastructures.
The Innovation Act will be tabled together with the 28th Regime for innovative companies,
enabling entrepreneurs to establish and operate across the EU within 48 hours. The Scaleup
Europe Fund will by making
in Europe. It will be complemented by an expanded European Innovation Council and a
new European Innovation Investment Pact to mobilise institutional capital. The European
Corporate Network will foster stronger collaboration between corporate venture investors and
corporate procurers and startups, while the Blue Carpet Initiative and the Fair Labour
Mobility Package will attract global talent and remove barriers for mobile innovators. Through
the Lab to Unicorn Initiative, DG RTD will accelerate the commercialisation of research results
by strengthening university-based innovation ecosystems, including setting up European
Startup and Scaleup Hubs and new pro-innovation procurement measures will make public
markets more accessible to innovative SMEs. With the support of European Research Area (ERA)
the Charter of Access will be developed for industrial users to research and
technology infrastructures, including for startups and scaleups, and, where necessary, simplify
and harmonise diverging access and contractual conditions. Financial support will be provided to
afford access to AI computing facilities for startups. To measure the progress, the Commission
will propose a recommendation on the definition of startups, scaleups and innovative
companies, taking into account existing definitions of SMEs and small mid-caps. In addition, the
Commission will set up a European Startup and Scaleup Scoreboard that will measure, based
on a set of indicators the performance of the European and national startup and scaleup
ecosystems. Finally, the Commission will carry out an annual startup and scaleup survey to
assess the perception
environment over time.
Complementing these measures, DG RTD will also drive sector-specific innovation
acceleration through the Advanced Materials Act, targeting a strategic technological value
7

technological and industrial leadership
and commercial success
strategic autonomy. With exponential growth in the demand for advanced materials: critical for
energy, mobility, construction and electronics, and the twin digital and green transitions this Act,
will establish a comprehensive framework aligning research, innovation, scale-up and
manufacturing within a unified European value chain. Building on the 2024 Communication on
Advanced Materials for Industrial Leadership , the Act will reduce fragmentation, accelerate
market uptake, and set clear standards for investment, circularity and supply-chain resilience,
ensuring Europe not only invents breakthrough materials but also commercialises and scales
them within the Union. The economic security risk assessment of advanced materials will
provide insights in how the EU remains a critical and non-substitutable player in key technologies
and can limit or replace strategic dependencies, such as e.g. critical raw materials to strengthen
EU economic security. The Scientific Advice Mechanism (SAM) will provide guidance on how
advanced materials can enhance EU strategic autonomy and promote cross-sectoral innovation.
DG RTD will also contribute to revising the General Block Exemption Regulation (GBER),
simplifying and modernising State aid rules to enhance competitiveness and support the net-zero
transition.

promoting innovative health solutions and fostering clean,
sustainable economic growth
green and digital transitions

of R&I knowledge related to factors such as end-of-waste criteria, extended producer
responsibility schemes, public procurement initiatives, electronic waste and critical raw materials.
This Act will enable the free movement of circular products and materials, stimulate demand for
towards a truly circular economy. DG RTD will also support the broader Clean Industrial Deal
package through a dedicated EUR 600 million Horizon Europe call (2026 2027), the Clean
Energy Investment Strategy, the Industrial Accelerator Act and the Battery Booster Strategy,
ensuring that R&I accelerate the development and deployment of low-carbon technologies.
The revision of the Research Fund for Coal and Steel will further align this legacy instrument
Complimenting these initiatives, the European Group
on Ethics in Science and New Technologies (EGE) will provide guidance on how policymakers can
better address the economic, social, and ethical challenges of achieving a Just Green Transition.
DG RTD will also contribute to major sectoral transformations. The Strategic Research and
Innovation Agenda for the European automotive sector will underpin the transition towards
zero-emission and digital mobility, while the Industrial Maritime Strategy and the EU Port
Strategy will turn maritime and port ecosystems into drivers of sustainable growth and
industrial innovation. Building on the knowledge of the Mission on Adaptation to Climate Change,
DG RTD will also support the forthcoming European Integrated Framework for Climate
Resilience, ensuring that R&I strengthen climate preparedness and risk management.
DG RTD will deliver the European Investment Plan for Clinical Research to strengthen multi-
country clinical trials capacity and clinical research infrastructures, as well as promote a One
8

Health approach, linking human, animal and environmental health research to better address
future health challenges.
In the health, bioeconomy and life sciences, DG RTD will implement the Strategy for European
Life Sciences, support the updated EU Bioeconomy strategy and will contribute to the EU
Biotech Act II. These flagship initiatives in line statement for
European leadership on global health, will simplify regulation, foster investment and accelerate
the translation of life science research into new technologies, bioeconomy solutions and health
innovations. As part of the Bioeconomy Strategys implementation and to coordinate
international bioeconomy stakeholders, DG RTD will co-organise with the Irish Presidency of
the Council the Global Bioeconomy Summit (GBS2026) in October. Back-to-back, the
International Bioeconomy Forum, co-chaired by DG RTD, will steer workshops on research
and innovation in the bioeconomy.
Supporting the clean energy transition, DG RTD will co-lead with DG ENER the EU Fusion
Strategy, promoting public-private partnerships to accelerate fusion energy commercialisation.
DG RTD will also contribute to the Communication on Small Modular Reactors, promoting
these technologies as flexible, low-carbon complements to renewables for those Member States
choosing to include nuclear energy in their energy mix.
Finally, DG RTD will contribute to the Quantum Act, establishing Europe as a global leader in
quantum technologies, and to the Energy Omnibus, including the revision of the Energy Union
Governance Regulation (6) , which will simplify and modernise EU energy product legislation,
creating a more innovation-friendly regulatory environment. The SET Plan Progress Report
will accompany these efforts by assessing progress under the Energy Union research,
innovation and competitiveness pillar.
Specific Objective 1.4: Developing an enabling research
ecosystem building on the European Research Area (ERA)
and empowering scientific talents

to be adopted in 2026, aims to tackle long-standing challenges in the EU's research and
innovation system, including fragmented regulatory frameworks, uneven R&D investment, and
mechanisms to
support national commitments, strengthen coordination of investments and policies between the
EU and Member State; particularly in strategic priority areas; and improve research careers,

DG RTD will implement the European Strategy on Research and Technology
Infrastructures (7) to reinforce the backbone of Europe's R&I ecosystem. Key actions include
increased investments in facilities and services, improved access schemes, strengthened capacity
to attract and retain talents. DG RTD will also propose a revision of the ERIC Regulation focusing
on facilitating international participation and clarifying jurisdictions.

Chairs call under Horizon Europe ( 230 million) will fund up to 120 top researchers and research
managers, completed by the ERC plus Scheme and other initiatives to attract and retain world-
class talents.
A strategic focus for 2026 is the implementation of the European Research Area (ERA) Policy
Agenda 2025-2027, which was adopted by the Council in June 2025. This comprehensive
roadmap is key to delivering on the ERA priorities set out in the Pact for R&I in Europe, ensuring
a true liberty of movement for researchers and knowledge across the continent. DG RTD will
coordinate the delivery of the 11 structural policies and 8 ERA actions, focusing on
areas such as open science, ethics and research integrity, science for policy, research careers,
and knowledge valorisation. Implementation will foster greater transnational cooperation and
address challenges related to sustainability, competitiveness, and disparities in R&I opportunities
across the Union. Additionally, DG RTD will develop a European scheme on responsible licensing
principles and shared data-governance approach to facilitate greater cross-sectoral collaboration
while addressing research security considerations.
In 2026, DG RTD will continue leading the transition to a fully operational, secure and trustworthy
European Open Science Cloud (EOSC), with top research infrastructures and data repositories
providing integrated services and high-quality data to researchers, and in co-creation with
national research performing and funding organisations, DG RTD will also lead the transition of
Open Research Europe (ORE) into a collectively funded publishing platform.
Following a 2025 reality check on SSH, DG RTD will review internal process to further integrate
social sciences and humanities (SSH) into Horizon Europe to enhance societal impact, foster a
human-centric approach to science and ensure science benefits for European citizens. Finally, DG
RTD will contribute to the EU Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2030 through the adoption in 2026
of the Action Plan for women in research, innovation, and start-ups, which will outline
st attractive place for women to study and work
in R&I. The 2026 award ceremony for the EU Gender Equality Champions in R&I will inspire
institution to become excellent in gender equality in R&I by recognising inclusive practices.
General objective 2: A new era for European Defences
and Security
Specific objective 2.1: Enhancing research and innovation
capabilities for strategic and dual-use technologies
Europe must be ready to assume greater responsibility for its own security. Building on its strong
deploy strategic and dual use technologies that contribute both to civilian and defences
objectives.
In 2026, DG RTD will implement the new provisions of the defence mini-omnibus (8)
amending the current Horizon Europe Regulation regarding the European Innovation Council (EIC),
allowing the EIC to invest in dual-use and defence-related activities through the envisaged
amendment of the EIC Work Programme 2026. DG RTD will also launch a dual-use pilot call in
the 2026 Work Programme of the Research Fund for Coal and Steel (RFCS). In this context, it will
develop guidance to ensure that dual-use activities are conducted in full compliance with EU
ethical standards, transparency principles, and EU values.

This work will lay the foundation for a coherent and secure approach to dual-use research and
innovation in the next Framework Programme evolving
security and technological landscape. This will strengthen capacity to develop and
protect critical technologies, safeguarding strategic autonomy and competitiveness in a rapidly
changing global context.
DG RTD will also contribute to EU defence-related initiatives that benefit from the broader EU
R&I ecosystem, notably in support of the European Defence Readiness Roadmap, the
Defence Transformation Roadmap and the Preparedness Union Strategy, with a
particular focus on strengthening civil-defence cooperation.
General Objective 4: Sustaining our quality of life:
food security, water and nature
Specific objective 4.1: Supporting a competitive and resilient
agriculture, food system and protecting water and nature
In an era of mounting environmental challenges and evolving global food security needs, DG RTD
supports an integrated approach that positions Europe as a global leader in demonstrating that
prosperity and environmental protection are complementary imperatives for a thriving future.
DG RTD will lead the implementation of the Strategy for European Life Sciences, delivering
a Strategic Research and Innovation Agenda on Food Systems to foster competitive,
sustainable and sustainable food systems solutions. This will complement the
forthcoming Strategic Approach to R&I in Agriculture, Forestry and Rural Areas
developed under the Vision for Agriculture and Food (9). The Scientific Advice Mechanism (SAM)
will advise the Commission on the impact of ultra-processed food on health in response to the
Vision for Agriculture and Food, the European Life Sciences Strategy, and the Cardiovascular
Action Plan.
In parallel, DG RTD will lead two key R&I strategies that underpin Europe environmental resilience
and competitiveness: the Water Resilience Research and Innovation Strategy and the
European Ocean Research and Innovation Strategy (ORIS). The Water Resilience R&I
Strategy, a core component of the Water Resilience Strategy (10) builds on progress achieved
under the European Missions Restore our Oceans and Waters and Adaptation to Climate
Change will close critical knowledge gaps on European freshwater and marine systems, water
availability, and the water-energy-food-ecosystems nexus. By strategically deploying EU research
funds, it will accelerate innovation in water technologies and strengthen support for SMEs.
Complementing this, the ORIS will support the implementation of the European Ocean Pact (11).
ORIS will operationalise a source-to-sea approach and will complement the Water Resilience R&I
Strategy by improving coordination between marine, coastal and freshwater research. It will
strengthen the governance of the European ocean and water knowledge system, bridge the gap
between R&I, and channel investments towards the deployment of new solutions. In line with the
EU R&I programmes and the
advance the development of a competitive, sustainable and resilient blue economy. Furthermore,
DG RTD will co-lead the Ocean Observation Initiative - ensuring sustainability, greater
autonomy and coherence of the European Ocean Observation system, whilst supporting the

preparation and early implementation of the Ocean Act. In parallel, DG RTD will contribute to
the Vision 2040 for Fisheries and Aquaculture, promoting sustainable practices, innovation
stewardship. In 2026, major milestones will be achieved by the four EU Green Missions.
The Mission on Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities will see 103 labelled cities begin
implementing their Climate City Contracts with innovative financial instruments and partnerships
supported by the Mission Platform and the European Investment Bank. The Mission on
Adaptation to Climate Change will reach 300 regions and local authorities with technical

bottom-up research approaches that are place-based and collaborative, engaging stakeholders
to address specific soil health needs and challenges in real-world settings. The Mission "Restore
our Ocean and Waters" will achieve 300 demo-sites testing solutions for the restoration of the
ocean and waters and 1500 Charter actions.

General Objective 8: A modern high performing and
sustainable European Commission
Specific Objective 8.1: Providing high performing support to
implementation of EU R&I programmes
In 2026, in close collaboration with the other services, DG RTD will ensure the negotiation of the
two Commission proposals on the next framework programme for research and innovation and
on the next Euratom programme for research and training actions, as well as supporting the
discussions on the European Competitiveness Fund.
DG RTD will amend the Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026-27 to ensure that the
commitment to allocate 10% of the Horizon Europe budget to biodiversity is met. This
amendment will also support the transition towards the next Framework Programme, in particular
to prepare the approach of the Investment Journey.
DG RTD will also advance the evidence base for policymaking through key publications. The 2026
report will provide an

DG RTD will prepare the Single Basic Act (SBA) for the next generation of Joint Undertakings,
to be adopted end 2026. This act will provide the common legal and organisational framework
for institutionalised European partnerships under the new framework programme. The SBA will
streamline governance structures, ensure member contributions align with defined thresholds
and promote synergies, economies of scale and stronger ties across value chains and

assessment report on the EU Missions in 2026. To anticipate future technological trends, DG RTD
will conduct an analysis of emerging technologies as a pilot for the future Observatory of
Emerging Technologies to be implemented under the next European Competitiveness Fund.
Key Simplification and Implementation Activities and
Outputs in 2026
In 2026, DG RTD will pursue its efforts to simplify the implementation of Horizon Europe and to
objective of at least a 25 % reduction in administrative burden.
Building on the successful Implementation Dialogue with Commissioner Zaharieva, and the
follow up Reality Check, DG RTD will further enhance accessibility and efficiency of EU R&I
funding. Feedback collected from a wide range of stakeholders will guide the prioritisation and
roll-out of selected simplification measures focusing on simpler application and grant
management processes already in 2026 and 2027. Novel approaches, including partial
randomisation will be tested before broader implementation.
DG RTD will further expand the use of lump sums, which will reach 50% of the overall Horizon
Europe call budget in 2026 (12). This includes achieving over 95% lump sum coverage in Pillar 3,
particularly benefiting SMEs through the EIC whilst Pillar 2 will increase from 40% in 2025 to
55% in 2026 lump sums funding. This will eliminate financial reporting obligations for
approximately half of the beneficiaries under 2026 HE calls, leading to an estimated of 21% -
The Client Centricity Programme will remain a central vehicle for simplification, and new
mobile functionalities for expert management and partnering will be launched in the "EU
Funding & Me" app. DG RTD will also upgrade the eGrants suite to a future-ready architecture
through the reengineering of IT tools, containerization, move to microservices, configurability, and
progressive move to the Cloud in line with the Commission's Digital Strategy . In cooperation
with DG BUDG and the (CIC) will
advance the establishment of the Single Gateway to EU budget and funding services, as
foreseen in the draft Performance Regulation for the next MFF. The CIC will work in close
coordination with direct and shared management DGs as well as corporate IT governance. DG
RTD will also focus on first level of consolidation of operational services to support beneficiaries
for go to market activities.
14

Under the lead of DG BUDG, Secretariat General and DG HR, DG RTD will contribute to the cost
benefit analysis (CBA) for the direct programme implementation 2028-2034.
Two major initiatives under the 2026 Commission Work Programme have a strong simplification
dimension: The European Innovation Act will propose innovation-friendly governance, and
simplifications for startups and scaleups. The Advanced Materials Act will address simplification
stakeholders.
In addition, the revision of the legal framework of the Research Fund for Coal and Steel
will propose simplification measures and facilitate investments. Outdated provisions will be
repealed or adapted, and research objectives will be less prescriptive, thus providing a clearer
and more coherent legal framework that will allow a better and more flexible approach for
fostering innovation and competitiveness in the sectors. This will provide for an improved and
more attractive funding system that will be aligned to overall EU funding landscape, with
simplified legal documents, streamlined calls, and the possibility to provide larger fundings.
The revision of the Commission Recommendation on the Safe and Sustainable by Design
(SSbD) chemicals and materials framework will also contribute to simplification by
introducing simplified approaches for safety and sustainability assessments, as starting points
for informed decision-making of businesses. This voluntary support tool can thus become more
beneficial for SMEs, including startups and scaleups, during the early innovation stages and when
resources are limited. By applying SSbD early, it can help businesses with a better cost
effectiveness of their innovation process and greater regulatory compliance and thus a shorter
time-to-market.
Finally, DG RTD will report on its second Reality Check on
implementation of non-financial obligation on Social Science and Humanities
conducted in November 2025 identifying ways to simplify SSH
integration across applications, evaluations, and project implementation and barriers and
benefits for researchers and applicants.
Progress on key policy objectives, enforcement and implementation made in the field of
startups, research and innovation during the year will be reported in the annual progress
report on simplification, implementation, and enforcement in 2026.
Details of the planned outputs can be found in Annex 1.

PART 3. A modern and sustainable public
administration: outputs in 2026
The internal control framework supports sound management and decision-making. In particular,
it ensures that risks to the achievement of objectives are addressed and reduced to acceptable
levels through cost-effective controls. DG RTD has established an internal control system tailored
to its particular characteristics and circumstances. The effective functioning of this internal
control system will be assessed on an ongoing basis throughout the year and will be subject to
an annual assessment covering all internal control principles.
Human resource management
To maintain a skilled, diverse, and motivated workforce, DG RTD will build on the foundations
established through the 2024 2025 HR Strategy and Action Plan a new RTD HR Action Plan
in 2026. This plan will consolidate achievements and introduce new measures supporting staff
growth, collaboration, and engagement across the DG, taking into account the results of the 2025
Staff Survey. Key actions in 2026 will include:
• Finalisation and roll-out of the new RTD HR Action Plan (2026 2027), aligning
local priorities with corporate objectives and focusing on staff engagement and gender
balance indicators.
• Launch of the RTD Job Shadowing initiative, enabling colleagues to gain insights into
different job profiles, broaden their understanding of RTD activities, and strengthen cross-
unit collaboration.
• Targeted talent management initiatives, such as the RTD Talent Development
Programme that was piloted in 2025 as well as the ongoing Learning & Development
strategy, tailored training plans, and a strengthened onboarding and mentorship schemes
for newcomers.
• Further investment in staff wellbeing, through awareness-raising actions on
activities and available support mechanisms, anti-harassment measures, and initiatives
actively promoting an open and respectful workplace.
• Measures to promote diversity and equality like inclusive recruitment and talent-
management practices in line with DG HR guidance, awareness-raising and training on
unconscious bias and inclusive leadership as well as promotion of flexible working
arrangements supporting work-life balance and diverse needs.
• Enhanced staff engagement through all-
and interactive exchanges with the Director-General, to foster transparency and a strong
sense of belonging.
DG RTD will monitor progress through the corporate staff engagement indicator and gender
balance indicators.

campaign will continue in 2026, focusing on specialized training for specific job categories.

Data Management: In anticipation of the upcoming MFF and its streamlined funding framework,
DG RTD will continue to expand its data management practices (key area #1) to include data
from all grants, not limited to R&I. The integration of diverse data sources aims to improve
adherence to corporate guidelines and enhance accessibility throughout the DG and the
Commission. We plan to explore metadata catalogue solutions to better organise and enhance
accessibility of our data resources, thereby supporting systematic documentation and reporting
practices, and aiding integration with other funding instruments. This will strengthen the
organised inventory of datasets, enable direct linkages to the EC Data Catalogue and enhance
the transparency of our data assets.
By 2026, we anticipate making substantial progress in pinpointing data stewards and owners,
building upon the governance bodies and structures that were revamped in 2025 to more

defining roles, ownership, and responsibilities (key area #2), establishing accountability, and

DG RTD will continue its commitment to data quality and FAIRness (key area #3) by

enhancing data skills will empower our workforce to actively contribute to the Commission's

Sound financial management
In 2026, Horizon Europe will operate at full capacity alongside Horizon 2020's legacy. Payment
expenditure will flow to Executive Agencies, Joint Undertakings, Public-Public-Partnerships, the
European Investment Bank, and Euratom Programme grants and contracts. Both Horizon 2020
and Horizon Europe feature tailored ex-ante control measures using objective criteria to
manage risks. The Research & Innovation Network of Ex ante Control practitioners (RINEC)
enhance these controls' efficiency and effectiveness. Ex-post control for grants
management is largely centralized in the Common Audit Service (CAS) for the R&I family.
The internal control system of DG Research and Innovation is designed to maintain error rates
within an acceptable range. For Horizon 2020, the goal remains reducing the cumulative error
rate to near 2%. However, for Horizon Europe, the objective is to achieve a cumulative error
rate below 2%. The Common Implementation Centre in cooperation with DG BUDG and the
Internal Audit Service has defined simplification actions including increased use of simplified
forms of funding (lump sums and unit costs) and targeted communication for "error-prone"
beneficiaries like SMEs, as well as improvements to the personnel cost wizard. The 2026-2027
work Programme increases lump sum funding up to 50% of the Pillar II call budget. The optional
unit cost for personnel costs launched in 2024 offers significant potential for simplification and
reduction of errors.
Enhanced training for project officers and External Audit Firms performing audits on behalf of
the Commission focuses on common errors as part of the client-centric approach launched in
2023. It should be noted that although the implementation of these actions is underway, their
positive effect in the form of reduction in the multiannual error rate may take time to materialise.
For indirect management and activities delegated to Executive Agencies, DG RTD relies on the
implementing bodies' reports. In 2026, the CIC will continue to refine the supervision framework
18

for Executive Agencies, Joint Undertakings, and other bodies implementing Horizon Europe,
strengthening data-driven monitoring and aligning best practices in close cooperation with all
lead parent DGs. In particular, building on the 2025 pilot, an Executive Agency dashboard will be
rolled out. The CIC will also oversee the final stages of the triennial evaluation for 2021-2024,
in close cooperation with all lead parent DGs that will conclude with a report to Council, European
Parliament and ECA. EIC Fund supervision is carried out, among other, through EIB reporting as
set out in the Contribution Agreement, in compliance with article 154 of the Financial Regulation.
The supervision also includes the controls for non-expenditure items, i.e., assets, liabilities and
off-balance sheets. The overall management of the EIC Fund has benefited from the complete
implementation of the actions resulting from the IAS recommendations. Any potential IAS
recommendations issued as part of the recently performed audit on grant preparation and award
decision of some of the EIC features will be reviewed and followed up as required. The CIC helps
reduce costs based on economies of scale and leverages the impact of simplification,
synergies, and harmonisation.
The estimated risk at payment for cost-based expenditure (1): Concerning the Risk at payment
for Horizon Europe grants, for which no representative error rate for Horizon Europe was available
in 2024 (2) but will be made available by end 2025, the target for 2029 is to represent less than
2% of relevant expenditure. The estimated risk at payment for Horizon 2020 grants in 2025 is
currently calculated at 3.92%. The target is to keep it as close as possible to 2% (between 2%
and 5%).

Fraud risk management
DG RTD manages fraud risk through two complementary strategies aligned with the 2023
Commission Anti-Fraud Strategy (CAFS) Action Plan (3):
- DG Research and Innovation Anti-Fraud Strategy (DG RTD AFS) addresses fraud risks
in non-grant management expenditure areas including procurement, financial instruments, prizes,
expert management. Updated in December 2022, it promotes awareness and training on ethics
issues, research integrity, and anti-fraud measures. In 2026, DG RTD will ensure that all
newcomers receive adequate training on their ethics obligations and anti-fraud measures.
Moreover, the 2026 update of the DG RTD AFS will reflect the switch to indirect management
of the EIC Accelerator investment component and incorporate possible findings from 2025 ECA
audit on the -fraud strategy.
- The Common Anti-Fraud Strategy (RAFS) addresses fraud risks related to grant
management in the implementation of R&I programmes. Because of the multi-DG dimension of
the R&I Framework Programme, the Common Audit Service (CAS) coordinates this strategy,
suggests actions, and chairs the Fraud and Irregularities in Research (FAIR) Committee. The CAS
will continue to collaborate closely with OLAF in case selection, investigations, and its yearly
financial monitoring exercises.
